provenance.v2_change: B1-E5 toolbox v2: adds the near_miss criterion (correction of the P4 miss on the 7017-ctrl type, 'same score, variable trajectory') + the discriminator semantic-narrowing clause; the strict v1 criterion and every registered row are kept unchanged; machine discriminator = train/probe_composite_signature.py (invariant_class_v2)

criterion.name: manager_invariant_row
preconditions: worker sha256 byte-identical in both archives
manager sha256 differs between the archives (H=0f2264… vs M29=894413…)
protocol deterministic=true and identical seed sets (eval_assembled v3, argmax_with_action_masks)
criterion.rule: the two rows of the same seed are exactly equal on all 13 fields below (numbers at their archived face value, no tolerance)
criterion.semantics: under deterministic evaluation, all 13 fields equal (incl. mode_seq character by character and overrides) ⇒ both managers produced the same decision sequence on that seed ⇒ the seed's result is insensitive to swapping the manager; if the score is low, the failure lies in the worker/environment layer, not the manager (a pure worker-level failure test, one-sided: the converse 'not invariant ⇒ the manager is to blame' does not hold)
criterion.one_sided_warning: not invariant ⇏ manager is the main cause; invariant ⇏ healthy worker (it only clears the manager)

near_miss_criterion.name: manager_invariant_near_miss_v2
near_miss_criterion.prereg_ref: docs/prereg/PREREG-B1-bundled-eval-infra.md E5 (from P4: correction of the missed 7017-ctrl type)
near_miss_criterion.rule: outcome fields (outcome_fields) exactly equal ∧ at least one trajectory field (trajectory_fields) differs ⇒ near_miss (near miss: 'same score, variable trajectory'); all 13 fields equal still gives strict_invariant (v1 criterion unchanged); outcome fields already differ ⇒ variable (trajectory variable)
near_miss_criterion.exemplar: 7017-ctrl: both managers have ret 58.3 but 4 trajectory fields such as farm_tau/windows/mode_seq differ (recorded in P4 residual_seed_checks)
near_miss_criterion.triage_semantics: post-hit triage of the composite signature (PREREG-B1 D3): 'variable (trajectory variable)' → F-lock type; 'strict_invariant or near_miss (invariant, incl. near miss)' → worker-damage candidate

semantic_narrowing_clause: discriminator semantic-narrowing clause (from P7 ruling 3, enacted in B1-E5): 'manager invariant' only shows 'swapping the examiner does not help', not 'the loss is unrecoverable' -- every verdict that cites it must carry this caveat

low_abs.rationale: throne-H reference (v32-ref-launch) ret Q1=55.19, rounded to 50 as the registered threshold

regression.rule: ret − ref_H(seed) <= -30.0 (7000 pool only, reference = same seed in v32-ref-launch)
regression.rationale: excludes the throne's chronic seeds; Δ≤−30 counts as a regression beyond noise

classification.chronic_seed: invariant ∧ low_abs ∧ ¬regression (the throne reference is equally low: a chronic seed inherited from the lineage)

residual_seed_checks.7013: sov invariant with ret=-2.88 (Δ=-91.75) ⇒ pure worker level, specific to sov ✓; on the ctrl side 7013 is manager-sensitive (H 23.1 vs M29 225.6), not on the ctrl list ✓
residual_seed_checks.7021: ctrl invariant with ret=-1.12 (Δ=-75.22) ⇒ pure worker level, specific to ctrl ✓; on the sov side 7021 is not invariant (72.1 vs 72.3) ✓
residual_seed_checks.7017: not caught by the strict invariant criterion: the two sov managers differ on 9 fields; the two ctrl managers both have ret 58.3 but 4 trajectory fields (farm_tau/windows/mode_seq) differ ⇒ a 'same score, variable trajectory' near miss; all four configurations score low (55.9-63.0 vs reference 258.6), which still supports a worker-level conclusion, but it needs the near-miss criterion or a P5 replay to confirm
residual_seed_checks.7007: sov invariant, ret=85.46, Δ=-64.04 ⇒ pure worker-level regression, matching the FORENSICS finding 'large loss outside the sov list, 7007 −64' ✓
residual_seed_checks.v31_ref_vs_v32_ref: launch/science: all 32 rows identical field by field, confirming the FORENSICS 'relabel' finding ✓

caveats: 7022 (7000 pool) and 9001 (9000 pool) are dead seeds: the rows are invariant to both the manager and the worker (sov/ctrl/throne identical field by field), ret≈-5.7, 0 kills, all F -- environment-level bad seeds; any list statistic should exclude them or report them separately
9009 (9000 pool) is a high-score invariant (ret=215.08, depth=2, died=true): invariant ≠ low score; the discriminator only labels the low-score subset 'pure worker level'
near-miss criterion (proposed for toolbox v2): ret and depth/died/kills equal but trajectory fields differ ⇒ a 'same-score row'; 7017-ctrl is of this kind
the criterion depends on deterministic=true and argmax; it cannot be used under any sampled evaluation
the s16 pool has only the H manager and no paired archives, so it is outside this registry
